newsitem.title: USA: US lawmaker says extending NAFTA would be mistake.
newsitem.headline: US lawmaker says extending NAFTA would be mistake.

text.p: House Democratic Leader Richard Gephardt said Wednesday that extending NAFTA to bring in Chile would be a mistake because the current agreement is not working.

In a speech to the Economic Strategy Institute, Gephardt said he believes the North American Free Trade Agreement -- which joins the United States, Mexico and Canada in a free trade zone -- needs fixing before Congress gives President Clinton new authority to negotiate trade agreements.
"I believe it would be a fundamental mistake to simply extend NAFTA," Gephardt said. "It simply isn't working."

The biggest flaw, he said, was NAFTA's failure to adequately address workers' rights. Mexican wages have failed to rise under NAFTA and living conditions of the Mexican people have not improved, he said. Environmental laws have been weakened, he said.

"I am unwilling to support new trade negotiations that do not address these fundamental flaws by including labor rights and the environment as chapters in the core of the agreement equal in stature and force and linked to investment and trade," he said.

Disagreement between Democrats and Republicans over whether labor and environmental issues should be included in trade negotitions has delayed so-called fast track trade negotiation legislation. Republicans who control Congress oppose including labor and environment issues in the fast track authority. Democrats want it included.
U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky told the group earlier the administration was working to build a consensus in Congress on fast track before sending to Congress proposed legislation.
